findings.title: DSA-2026-451: Security Update for Dell Enterprise SONiC Distribution Vulnerabilities
findings.summary_md: Dell's advisory lists Enterprise SONiC Distribution versions prior to 4.6.1 as affected and version 4.6.1 as the remediated build. It describes the release as addressing multiple proprietary-code vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-103782, an argument injection flaw that a low-privileged remote attacker could use to run arbitrary commands. The advisory was published six days before the story was first seen.

findings.title: EUVD-2026-133149 (CVE-2026-103782)
findings.summary_md: ENISA's vulnerability database records CVE-2026-103782 in Dell Enterprise SONiC Distribution with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.9 and vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H. The record describes an argument injection issue affecting versions before 4.6.1 that can lead to arbitrary command execution. The entry was published two days before the story was first seen.

findings.title: CVE-2026-103782 - Vulnerability Details - OpenCVE
findings.summary_md: OpenCVE published its CVE-2026-103782 record on 23 November 2026 and classifies the issue as argument injection leading to remote code execution in Dell Enterprise SONiC Distribution. The entry gives a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.9, lists EPSS as unavailable, and shows the CVE as not listed in CISA KEV. Those fields were recorded before the story appeared and say nothing about later exploitation.

findings.title: Dell Enterprise SONiC 4.6.1 Fixes 13 Flaws, Including CVSS 9.9 RCE
findings.summary_md: SecurityOnline reports that Dell SONiC 4.6.1 fixes 13 proprietary-code vulnerabilities in Enterprise SONiC Distribution. It identifies CVE-2026-103782 as a CVSS 9.9 argument injection flaw and says two critical issues in the set allow arbitrary command execution on affected switches. The article was published at 01:00:41 UTC on 25 November 2026, about six hours before the story was first seen.
